page.layout: One column of text on the page, with the printed page number top right and the running head "LATINA." top centre. No marginal notes. The signature "c 3" stands at the foot below the last line.

main_text.l: tivo. Comparativus autem, addito or, pro communi
genere, & us, pro neutro: ut, à Docti, gelehrt / Doctior,
Doctius, à tenui, dünn / tenuior, tenuius, à feli-
ci, glückselig / felicior, felicius. Superlativus, addito
issimus, pro masculino, issima pro foemino, issimum
pro neutro: ut, doctissimus, doctissima, doctissimum.
Si tamen positivus desinat in er, superlativus mascu-
linus fit, addito rimus, foemininus addito rima, neu-
ter rimum: ut niger, schwarz / nigerrimus, nigerri-
ma, nigerrimum. Quidam positivi formant Superla-
tivos in limus: ut facilis, leicht / facilimus.
Agilis, schnel und fertig / agilimus. Gracilis, dünn und
mager / gracilimus. Humilis, niederträchtig und de-
mütig / humilimus. Similis, gleich / similimus.
Bonus, gut / melior, besser / optimus, der beste.
Malus, böß /
pejor, erger / pessimus, der ergste.
Magnus, groß / major, größer / maximus, der größte.
Parvus, klein / minor, kleiner / minimus, der
kleinste. Et parvissimus, Lucretio.
Multus, | plurimus.
Multa, | plurima.
Multum, viel / plus, mehr / plurimum, das meiste.
Vetus, alt / veterior, elter / veterrimus, der elteste.
Sacer, heilig / magis sacer, sacerrimus.
Frugi, hänßlich / frugalior, frugalissimus.
Pius, Gottsfürchtig / magis pius, maxime pius.
Piissimus apud Diomedem, Senecam & Cuttium re-
peritur: Et apud quosdam alios pientissimus.
Reliqua omnia, vocalem ante us vel is habentia
per magis & maxime describuntur: praeter tenuis,
tenuior, & strenuus, strenuior.
Dexter, recht / oder glückhafftig / dexterior, dextimus.
Nequam, schalckhafft / nequior,
nequissimus.
Maturus, zeitig oder reiffe / maturior, maturrimus
& maturissimus.

page.notes: The asterisk-like mark beside "strenuus" in the right margin is a stray printer's mark, not a note, so it is left out. The symbol before "ottsfürchtig" is a printed sign, not a letter; it is left out and the German word is kept. "Superlativus" forms of "issimus" appear with a long-s-like letter in print and are written as plain s. The German glosses are in black letter and marked bl. Some German words are at the edge of legibility, notably "gelehrt", "glückselig" and "erger"; they are copied as seen and may be off. The printed "maturrimus" is left as printed.
